Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the final innings of Ashes 2023! England players walk out to the field as Aussie openers, David Warner and Usman Khawaja make their way out to the middle too. Stuart Broad has taken his hat off and will start the proceedings with the ball. David Warner awaits at the other end, here we go...
... FINAL INNINGS ....

Talking of cricket, England have added 6 runs this morning and the pitch still is pretty good to bat on. However, Aussies need to be more proactive than they were in the first innings and a good start will be critical in their pursuit here. Todd Murphy and Mitchell Starc have picked four wickets each to give Australia a chance here and let's see how things pan out. Also, on this day, in 2011, Stuart Broad picked up an hattrick against India in a Test match. It wil be quite a moment if he does that in his final game too. Stay tuned for Australia’s final reply.

That’s it! England have been bowled out for 395 and Australia need 384 runs to win this series by a 3-1 margin. We have seen the last of the Anderson-Broad pair with bat in hand but they would be itching to get their hands on that red cherry now and hunt down the Aussies in tandem for one last time. Broad has retired but there is uncertainty over Anderson’s future too, so let’s embrace the spectacle that is coming our way.

OUT! LBW! Todd Murphy gets his fourth of the game and England's innings has come to an end within two overs of Day 4! Todd Murphy loops this one full and pitching just outside off. The ball comes into the stumps with the angle as James Anderson goes for the reverse sweep once again. He does not connect this time and the ball hits him on his pad. A loud appeal from the bowler and the umpire takes a long time before raising his finger. James Anderson goes for the review and replays show that the ball is quite far from the bat. Ball Tracking has umpires call on wickets hitting and the on-field decision stands. England have been bowled out for 395 and Stuart Broad remains unbeaten in his last Test inning as the set the visitors a target of 384.

Commentary.Commentary: So, we are all set for Day 4! England have not declared and Anderson-Broad are walking down the stairs as Aussies are ready with their Guard of Honour! Stuart Broad wanted Anderson to accompany him but Anderson stopped and has allowed Broad to soak in all the applause. Stuart Broad will take the strike as well as Mitchell Starc starts the proceedings with the ball. Here we go...

As far as Australia is concerned, they did not do their chances any good on Day 3 of this Test match. England came out with their typical Bazball antics and scored runs at almost five runs per over to put Australia in a tricky position now. Root, Crawley, and Bairstow all scored runs at a rapid rate and though Australia found ways to take wickets, they need their batters to step up now to register an unlikely win here. Aussies would first have to take England’s final wicket though and it would be quite a spectacle to watch James Anderson and Stuart Broad bat together one final time in Test cricket. However, there is a possibility that rain might ruin that spectacle as the weather does not look promising. If we get a delayed start to the proceedings, England might just declare and not take any chances after what happened in Manchester. Get ready for a roller-coaster day at a jam-packed Kennington Oval.

Hello and a very warm welcome, folks! We are ready for what could be a pretty emotional day at the historic Kennington Oval. If this turns out to be the last day of the Ashes 2023, it will also be the final day for Stuart Broad in international cricket. The man is a legend of the game and only the second pacer to take more than 600 wickets in Test cricket. The match is also poised beautifully for him to waive his magic as England are 377 ahead with just one wicket in hand and it will all come down to the English bowling group. The pair of Anderson-Broad will also be seen one last time in Test cricket and it promises to be a day full of nostalgia.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from another riveting Day of Test cricket action where England have completely changed the game and are way ahead at the moment. They have a lot of time barring any rain to level the series while Australia need something really special to get a favourable result. Before we bid you farewell, there is big news coming through as STUART BROAD HAS ANNOUNCED HIS RETIREMENT claiming that this will be his last game of cricket. The man who recently crossed 600 wickets in Test cricket has chosen a big stage to hang his boots as England hunt for a win to level the Ashes series. This makes the action on Day 4 of this fifth and final Test even more intriguing. The first ball will be bowled at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT) but you can join us well in adavance for the build-up. Cheers!

The hosts still have one wicket left and will look to extend the lead even more on Day 4. Australia, on the other hand, were pretty lacklustre with their bowling effort and things weren't happening for them. They conceded a lot of runs and let England build several big partnerships throughout the batting order. They struggled hard for two sessions to pick up wickets but made a spirited comeback in the third session and picked up five wickets. Todd Murphy was brilliant and picked up three wickets while Mitchell Starc once again claimed a four-fer. Pat Cummins and Josh Hazlewood chipped in with one but they still have a lot to do and their batters will have to be at their best to chase down any target that will be set. England will be hoping their final pair can push them beyond the 400-run mark for some psychological advantage.

England got off to a great start courtesy of both the openers Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley keeping the runs flowing. They notched up another half-century opening stand and saw out the first hour. Duckett got out on 42 but Crawley carried on with Ben Stokes and built another big partnership before the former got dismissed on 73 at the start of the second session. That did not affect them as Joe Root and Ben Stokes didn't have much trouble and scored runs pretty easily. Stokes holed out after getting to a start but Root stayed there and breezed to 91 runs but unfortunately missed out on his hundred. Jonny Bairstow looked like a man on a mission and smashed 78 runs off just 103 balls to help the hosts to get past the 300-run mark. Moeen Ali made a decent contribution despite his injury but the lower order couldn't do much.

It is called the 'moving day' and this game has certainly moved massively in favour of the hosts as they lead by a huge margin of 377 runs. The Aussies looked tired out there as they weren't able to execute their plans and despite a late comeback in the last session, they find themselves way behind in this game with a lot of time still left.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session of Day 3 as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The Australian players take their respective positions on the field as Joe Root and Jonny Bairstow stride out to the middle to continue their partnership for England. Todd Murphy has the ball in his hand and is ready to begin proceedings. ... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ....

Zak Crawley looked really ominous going into Lunch but could not make an impact after the break as he edged one to Steven Smith at slip to bring an end to the 61-run second-wicket partnership in 57 deliveries. Joe Root came out to bat and looked like a man on a mission as he scored freely from the word go. He added 73 runs in 79 balls with Ben Stokes for the third wicket as he reached his half-century in just 42 deliveries. The English skipper perished in the quest for some quick runs 8 runs short of his fifty and Harry Brook could not follow up his first-inning performance with another good score. Jonny Bairstow came out with destruction on his mind as he raced to 34 in 35 balls and England seem to be cruising at the moment. Do join us at 8.30 pm IST (3 pm GMT) for more entertainment in the final session of Day 3.

SESSION SUMMARY - 135 runs and 3 wickets in 24 overs. Australia have put in a much better performance in this session with the ball but with England scoring at well above 5 runs per over, the game seems to be creeping away from them. Pat Cummins struck in the second over post Lunch but the visitors could not get a breakthrough for almost an hour after that. Todd Murphy managed to dismiss the England skipper after the drinks break and Josh Hazlewood got a wicket in the very next over to give Australia some hope of restricting the scoring rate. That was not the case however as the hosts continued playing their shots without losing any further wickets swelling the lead to 253. England came out to bat in a typical manner as they looked to score runs quickly and overcame the deficit of 12 runs in the first over itself. Ben Duckett was off the blocks quickly as he scored 42 runs in 55 balls in the 79-run opening partnership before edging one to the keeper. He will be disappointed in missing out after a good start but the momentum was not lost as Zak Crawley took over from his partner and began scoring at a quick rate. Ben Stokes promoted himself to number 3 and added a 51-run unbeaten partnership with Crawley as England now lead by 118 runs. A chastening session for the visitors and they will be hoping to get some footing in this game before the hosts plunder their way to a strong second-innings total. Do join us at 6.10 pm IST (12.40 pm GMT) to find out how the second session of Day 3 plays out.

SESSION SUMMARY - 130 runs and 1 wicket in 25 overs. What a session of Test cricket we have witnessed but this is not the kind of red-ball cricket we have witnessed over the years! This English side have shown that they know no fear and when Zak Crawley thumped the first ball to the fence to the delight of the crowd, it was evident that the visitors were going to be up against it. The Aussie fast bowlers tried their best to get an early wicket but were up against two openers who had the freedom to be positive and play their shots. Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins conceded boundaries far too easily releasing any pressure that was being built by Josh Hazlewood from the other end. They got some respite at the end of the 17th over when Starc managed to draw first blood but it has been all about England since then.
